title: Galois Group of Xˡ−p at Prime Degree: the Affine Lower Bound ℓ(ℓ−1) ∣ |Gal| via Free Coprimality
description: A new direct child of the parent metacyclic-bracket entry, specializing it uniformly to PRIME degrees ℓ. The parent's coprime sharpening n·φ(n) ∣ |Gal(Xⁿ−p/ℚ)| needs a per-n check that gcd(n,φ(n)) = 1, which the parent verifies one case at a time (n = 3, n = 5) with explicit `by decide`. This entry removes the case analysis for the entire family of prime degrees at once via a single number-theoretic observation: for prime ℓ, φ(ℓ) = ℓ−1, and ℓ is coprime to ℓ−1 because they are CONSECUTIVE integers (coprime_prime_totient) — no `decide`, no per-ℓ work. Hence the metacyclic lower bound reads uniformly ℓ·(ℓ−1) ∣ |Gal(Xˡ−p/ℚ)| (gal_card_affine_lower_bound), the order of the affine group AGL(1,ℓ) = ℤ/ℓ ⋊ (ℤ/ℓ)ˣ that is the conjectured exact Galois group under genericity. Combined with the parent's symmetric-group upper bound this gives the two-sided bracket ℓ·(ℓ−1) ∣ |Gal| ∣ ℓ! (gal_card_prime_degree_bracket) and the numerical lower bound |Gal| ≥ ℓ·(ℓ−1) (gal_card_ge_affine), quadratic in the degree. The parent's scattered n = 3 (6 = |S₃|) and n = 5 (20 = |F₂₀|) examples become the special cases ℓ ∈ {3,5} of one theorem; the new prime degree ℓ = 7 (42 = 7·6 ∣ |Gal| ∣ 5040) is recorded as a concrete instance. The base entry's n = 4 is excluded precisely because 4 is not prime (gcd(4,φ(4)) = 2 ≠ 1), explaining why it needed a separate real-embedding argument. 4 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: The Galois group of $X^n - p$ over $\mathbb{Q}$ (prime $p$) is metacyclic, sitting in $1 \to C_n \to \mathrm{Gal} \to (\mathbb{Z}/n)^\times \to 1$ with conjectured order $n\,\varphi(n)$ under genericity. The parent entry proves the divisibility bracket $n \mid |\mathrm{Gal}|$, $\varphi(n) \mid |\mathrm{Gal}|$, $|\mathrm{Gal}| \mid n!$, and sharpens to the full product $n\,\varphi(n) \mid |\mathrm{Gal}|$ when $\gcd(n, \varphi(n)) = 1$ — but it checks that coprimality one degree at a time ($n = 3$, $n = 5$). At a PRIME degree $\ell$ the coprimality is structural rather than computational: $\varphi(\ell) = \ell - 1$, and consecutive integers are always coprime. The metacyclic order then specializes to $\ell(\ell-1) = |\mathrm{AGL}(1, \ell)|$, the affine group $\mathbb{Z}/\ell \rtimes (\mathbb{Z}/\ell)^\times$, conjectured to be the exact Galois group of a prime-degree radical extension.
overview.problemStatement: Show that for every prime degree $\ell$ and prime $p$, the coprimality hypothesis of the parent's metacyclic sharpening is automatic (consecutive-integer coprimality of $\ell$ and $\ell - 1 = \varphi(\ell)$), so the affine order divides the Galois order uniformly: $\ell(\ell-1) \mid |\mathrm{Gal}(X^\ell - p/\mathbb{Q})|$. Combine with the parent's $S_\ell$-embedding upper bound to obtain the two-sided bracket $\ell(\ell-1) \mid |\mathrm{Gal}| \mid \ell!$ and the numerical lower bound $|\mathrm{Gal}| \ge \ell(\ell-1)$.
overview.proofStrategy: (1) coprime_prime_totient: rewrite $\varphi(\ell) = \ell - 1$ (Nat.totient_prime), then $\mathrm{Coprime}\,\ell\,(\ell-1)$ via Nat.Prime.coprime_iff_not_dvd reduced to $\ell \nmid (\ell - 1)$, discharged by $0 < \ell - 1 < \ell$ (Nat.le_of_dvd + omega). (2) gal_card_affine_lower_bound: feed the free coprimality into Nat.Coprime.mul_dvd_of_dvd_of_dvd over the parent's $\ell \mid |\mathrm{Gal}|$ and $\varphi(\ell) \mid |\mathrm{Gal}|$, then rewrite $\varphi(\ell) = \ell - 1$. (3) gal_card_prime_degree_bracket: pair the lower bound with the parent's $|\mathrm{Gal}| \mid \ell!$. (4) gal_card_ge_affine: Nat.le_of_dvd against Fintype.card_pos. Concrete examples instantiate $\ell \in \{3, 5, 7\}$.
keyInsights: **Coprimality is structural at prime degree, not computational.** The parent verifies $\gcd(n, \varphi(n)) = 1$ per case with `by decide`; for prime $\ell$ it is automatic because $\varphi(\ell) = \ell - 1$ and $\ell, \ell-1$ are consecutive integers. One lemma replaces an unbounded family of `decide` checks.

**The bound is the order of the affine group.** $\ell(\ell-1) = |\mathrm{AGL}(1, \ell)| = |\mathbb{Z}/\ell \rtimes (\mathbb{Z}/\ell)^\times|$ — the conjectured exact Galois group of $X^\ell - p$ under genericity. The lower bound thus says $\mathrm{Gal}$ contains a copy of the full affine group, with no genericity hypothesis.

**A quadratic numerical lower bound.** Turning divisibility into an inequality, $|\mathrm{Gal}(X^\ell - p/\mathbb{Q})| \ge \ell(\ell - 1)$ grows quadratically in the degree — far above the trivial $\ell \mid |\mathrm{Gal}|$ kernel bound.

**Why n = 4 is excluded.** The base $D_4$ entry's degree $4$ is not prime: $\gcd(4, \varphi(4)) = \gcd(4, 2) = 2 \ne 1$, so consecutive-integer coprimality does not apply and the bracket gives only $\mathrm{lcm}(4, 2) = 4 \mid |\mathrm{Gal}|$. This is exactly why $n = 4$ needed a separate real-embedding argument while every prime degree is handled uniformly here.

sections.title: Overview: the affine lower bound at prime degree
sections.summary: Module docstring recalling the parent's metacyclic bracket and coprime sharpening, then stating the prime-degree specialization: free consecutive-integer coprimality gives ℓ·(ℓ−1) ∣ |Gal| uniformly, the order of AGL(1, ℓ).

sections.title: Imports and namespace
sections.summary: Imports Mathlib and the parent module Proofs.InverseGaloisD4OQ02 (source of n ∣ |Gal|, φ(n) ∣ |Gal|, |Gal| ∣ n!); opens the dedicated InverseGaloisExtensions.PrimeDegree sub-namespace and Polynomial notation.

sections.title: Part I — automatic coprimality of a prime with its totient
sections.summary: coprime_prime_totient: for prime ℓ, Coprime ℓ φ(ℓ). Rewrites φ(ℓ) = ℓ−1 and uses Nat.Prime.coprime_iff_not_dvd to reduce to ℓ ∤ (ℓ−1), discharged by 0 < ℓ−1 < ℓ. This is the free coprimality that makes the parent's metacyclic product bound apply at every prime degree without case analysis.

sections.title: Part II — the affine lower bound ℓ(ℓ−1) ∣ |Gal|
sections.summary: gal_card_affine_lower_bound combines the parent's kernel factor ℓ and quotient factor φ(ℓ) via Nat.Coprime.mul_dvd_of_dvd_of_dvd into ℓ·(ℓ−1) ∣ |Gal|. gal_card_prime_degree_bracket pairs it with the parent's |Gal| ∣ ℓ! upper bound; gal_card_ge_affine (Nat.le_of_dvd) yields the numerical lower bound |Gal| ≥ ℓ·(ℓ−1).

sections.title: Part III — concrete instances ℓ ∈ {3, 5, 7}
sections.summary: Recovers the parent's n = 3 (6 = |S₃|) and n = 5 (20 = |F₂₀|) as special cases of the single uniform theorem, and records the new prime degree ℓ = 7 (42 = 7·6 ∣ |Gal(X⁷−p)| ∣ 5040 = 7!).

conclusion.summary: Specialized the parent metacyclic bracket uniformly to prime degrees: for every prime ℓ and prime p, ℓ·(ℓ−1) ∣ |Gal(Xˡ−p/ℚ)| ∣ ℓ! and |Gal| ≥ ℓ·(ℓ−1), with the affine order ℓ(ℓ−1) = |AGL(1,ℓ)| dividing |Gal| because ℓ and φ(ℓ) = ℓ−1 are consecutive integers, hence automatically coprime — no per-degree `decide`. 4 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: Reorganizes the parent's per-case coprime examples (n = 3, n = 5) into one structural theorem covering all prime degrees, and supplies a quadratic numerical lower bound |Gal| ≥ ℓ(ℓ−1). It pinpoints why prime degrees are uniformly tractable while the composite base case n = 4 (gcd(4, φ(4)) = 2) is not, sharpening the boundary of what the verified divisibility bracket decides on its own.
openQuestions: Match the affine lower bound with an upper bound |Gal(Xˡ−p)| ≤ ℓ(ℓ−1) (linear disjointness of ℚ(ˡ√p) and ℚ(ζₗ)) to pin |Gal| = ℓ(ℓ−1) = |AGL(1,ℓ)| exactly for every prime degree ℓ, not just the squeeze-closed ℓ ∈ {2,3} where ℓ(ℓ−1) = ℓ!.
Realize the affine group AGL(1, ℓ) as an explicit subgroup of Gal(Xˡ−p/ℚ) (semidirect structure ℤ/ℓ ⋊ (ℤ/ℓ)ˣ), upgrading the divisibility ℓ(ℓ−1) ∣ |Gal| to a concrete group embedding.

Extend the consecutive-integer coprimality trick to prime-power degrees ℓ^k, where φ(ℓ^k) = ℓ^{k-1}(ℓ-1) shares the prime ℓ with the degree, so coprimality fails and only lcm(ℓ^k, φ(ℓ^k)) ∣ |Gal| survives.
